clue.text: Something hot knocked over holding, say, hot drink

indicators.note: holding means the reversed word wraps around the next piece
knocked over means turned upside down, so in this across clue the word is read backwards

parts.note: the sun is something hot
say means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: Someone spills a scalding drink, knocking over something hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something hot' and 'hot drink' share a word, but only the second is the definition; the first is the wordplay's star of the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Negus is an old hot drink of port or sherry mixed with water, sugar and spice.

clue.text: Spray blue rinse by accident

indicators.note: by accident means the letters fall into a random new order

explanation.surface: A hairdresser sprays a blue rinse by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A nebuliser is a device turning liquid medicine into a fine spray for inhaling.

clue.text: Great brain, one removed in group of organisms

indicators.note: removed means that letter is taken out of the word for great brain

parts.note: a genius is a great brain
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A genius gets excluded from a biology class.
explanation.definitionFit: In biological classification a genus is a group of related species.

clue.text: Written punishment?

parts.note: a grammatical unit of written words, which is also the penalty a judge pronounces

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a written unit of grammar and a court's punishment, a pun on two senses.

clue.text: Representing trauma, ask for the other illustrations

indicators.note: representing in the sense of presenting anew, so the letters of the following words are arranged differently

explanation.surface: A request to depict something traumatic in illustrations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the other' is a coy British euphemism for sex, so 'the other illustrations' is a sex manual with pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Indian text on lovemaking is famous for its explicit erotic pictures, a coy euphemism for sex being 'the other'.

clue.text: Eccentric yo-yos

indicators.note: a yo-yo goes down and comes back up, so the letters read the same in either direction

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An odd person keeps fiddling with yo-yos.
explanation.definitionFit: A kook is slang for an eccentric or crazy person.

clue.text: Pole keeps fit getting up to crispy breakfast

indicators.note: keeps means the word for pole holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: a mast is a pole

indicators.note: getting up means the word is reversed in this down clue

parts.note: able is a synonym of fit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Pole keeps fit by getting up to a crisp breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person keeping fit; it is a mast. In a down clue 'getting up' reads a word from the bottom upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Melba toast is very thin crisp toast, sometimes eaten at breakfast.

clue.text: Fish shop banking millions

indicators.note: banking means enclosing, as a bank holds money

parts.note: a salon is a shop, as a hair or beauty salon

explanation.surface: A fishmonger banks millions.
explanation.definitionFit: Salmon is a familiar fish, a large game and food fish.

clue.text: String of islands in a ring

parts.note: toll means ring, as a bell

explanation.surface: A chain of islands forms a circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like the shape of the reef but is the verb for a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a ring-shaped coral reef or chain of islets around a lagoon.

clue.text: Cook, then eat a fool — it smells of fruit

indicators.note: eat means the first word swallows the following pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: to boil is to cook
taken as written
nana is British slang for a fool, as in 'a right nana'

explanation.surface: Someone cooks and then eats a fool, the fruit pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fool' looks like the fruit-and-cream dessert, which suits the fruit theme, but it is British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Banana oil is the solvent isoamyl acetate, whose smell strongly resembles ripe bananas.

clue.text: Dance neither here nor there

definitions.meaning: a West Indian dance in which one bends backwards under a lowered bar
a state of uncertainty or being in between, as souls supposedly waiting outside heaven and hell

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the bar-ducking dance and an intermediate state of neglect or uncertainty, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Man introducing antiseptics where swelling's beginning to disappear

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for a swelling is removed

parts.note: a blister is a small swelling on the skin

explanation.surface: A man brings in antiseptics so that a swelling starts to go down.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Lister pioneered antiseptic surgery in the 1860s.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Lister was the British surgeon who introduced antiseptic methods into surgery.

clue.text: Party first in coquettish excitement

indicators.note: first in means take only the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: arousal is a state of excitement

explanation.surface: At a party, a flirt is the first to get excited.
explanation.definitionFit: A carousal is a noisy drinking party, a synonym of carouse.

clue.text: Tiny flier embarrassed top sailor

parts.note: red, as one blushing when embarrassed
an admiral is a top-ranking naval officer

explanation.surface: A small pilot embarrassed a senior naval officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The red admiral is a butterfly, a small flying insect.

clue.text: Alert speller stuffs Kentish lecturer

indicators.note: stuffs means one piece is packed inside another

parts.note: Kent is a county in South East England, so Kentish gives SE
a witch is someone who casts spells, a speller
a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: A spelling expert fills in for a lecturer from Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speller' looks like someone good at spelling but means a caster of spells. Kent is a county in South East England.
explanation.definitionFit: Switched-on is informal for alert, quick-witted and up to date.

clue.text: Instinct during schooling

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the morning'
tuition is schooling

explanation.surface: Gut feeling while being taught.
explanation.definitionFit: Intuition is instinctive understanding without conscious reasoning.

clue.text: Platform said to appear wobbly

indicators.note: wobbly means unsteady, so the letters of the word before are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A stage is reported to look unsteady.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised platform at the end of a hall, for speakers or dignitaries.

clue.text: Car part is to be given up, please

indicators.note: given up in a down clue means the word is reversed

parts.note: taken as written
to delight is to please

explanation.surface: A car component must be surrendered, if you please.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidelight is a small lamp at the front side of a car.

clue.text: When upset, cross to leave by stage exit

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the pair of words is read backwards together

parts.note: a rood is a cross, especially in a church
to part is to leave

explanation.surface: Upset, someone crosses to leave by the stage exit.
explanation.walkthrough: One indicator, 'When upset', turns the whole phrase 'cross to leave' round, so the two words come out in swapped order.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapdoor in a stage floor lets actors vanish from view, a way off the stage.

clue.text: Mild oath from screen idol taken the wrong way

indicators.note: taken the wrong way means read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a film star is a screen idol

explanation.surface: A film star's remark is misinterpreted.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Rats!' is a mild exclamation of annoyance, a minced oath.

clue.text: Knot was tangled in plant tip

indicators.note: in means the jumbled letters go inside the word for plant

parts.note: a herb is a plant

indicators.note: tangled means the letters of the word are knotted into a new order

parts.note: a tip is an end

explanation.surface: A knot was caught up in the tip of a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: A herb counts as a plant; the knot is a sailor's bend, and 'tangled' fits the knot picture while signalling the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawser bend is a sailor's knot for joining two heavy ropes.

clue.text: Legitimate target in hoopla, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: someone or something that may fairly be attacked or criticised
hoopla, tossing rings over prizes, is an example of a game played at a fair

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a fair target, and read literally names a fairground amusement like hoopla.

clue.text: Error picked up by vacuum cleaner?

definitions.meaning: a blunder or slip, especially by an actor
soft fibres and dust that a vacuum cleaner sucks up

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a mistake, as a fluffed line, and the light fibres a vacuum gathers.

clue.text: Lounge lizard's head twists round 180 degrees

indicators.note: turning round 180 degrees means the whole string faces the other way, read backwards
head means the first letter of the word lizard

parts.note: warps is a synonym of twists

explanation.surface: A lizard on a lounge chair twists its head right round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lounge lizard' looks like one phrase, but 'Lounge' alone is the definition. L plus WARPS turned round gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprawl is to lounge, lying or sitting with limbs spread out carelessly.

clue.text: Unknown isle supports a truthful state books fi ment

clue.text: Tie up a number of patients

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is reversed

parts.note: a draw is a tie in a match

explanation.surface: Bind a group of patients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tie up' looks like a phrasal verb meaning bind, but 'up' signals reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital ward is a room holding a number of patients.

clue.text: Almost two hundred countries taking one forward in alliance

parts.note: the United Nations has 193 member countries, almost two hundred
one is the Roman numeral I
on means forward, as in 'go on'

explanation.surface: Nearly two hundred nations bring one forward in a pact.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is an alliance or association formed for mutual benefit.

clue.text: Call for each boy to interrupt argument

indicators.note: to interrupt means the other pieces break into the middle of the word for call

parts.note: to ring is to call on the telephone
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone telephones so each boy can butt into a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'argument' looks like a quarrel but means a line of logic.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning is a chain of logical argument, a case made by thinking things through.

clue.text: Like some flycatchers, didn't manage to catch another insect

indicators.note: to catch means the word for not managing surrounds the insect

parts.note: failed means didn't manage
an ant is an insect, another besides the flies being caught

explanation.surface: A bird failed to catch one more insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantailed describes birds such as the fantail flycatchers, which spread their tails like fans.

clue.text: Orders to put clock back

indicators.note: put back means the word is reversed

parts.note: a timer is a clock

explanation.surface: Instructions to set the clock back an hour.
explanation.definitionFit: A remit is a set of instructions or terms of reference given to someone.
